title: Mounting fabric in a Q-snap frame
subtitle: The plastic snap frame that holds cloth without the ring mark a wooden hoop leaves.
excerpt: A Q-snap frame uses PVC pipes and clip-on clamps to hold fabric under even tension. No ring mark, no screw to lose, and it assembles in seconds.
sourceNotes: Technique is a modern development (PVC snap frames became standard in cross-stitch from the 1980s). Content synthesised from practitioner knowledge and consistent with the framing principles established in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

glossaryTerms.definition: The spring-loaded plastic clip that snaps over a Q-snap pipe to grip the fabric. Push it on over the fabric; push it off to release. Each clamp grips one side of the frame.

content.text: A Q-snap frame is a square or rectangular PVC pipe frame with clip-on clamps that grip the fabric along each side. It leaves no ring mark, holds large pieces without scrolling, and comes apart flat for storage. The key is gripping the fabric evenly on all four sides before tightening.

items.name: Fabric with at least 5 cm border around the design area

content.text: How to mount fabric in a Q-snap
Assemble the four pipe sides into the square frame. The corner joints push together firmly.
Lay the fabric face-up and centred over the frame on a flat surface.
over one side of the frame with the fabric beneath it. The clamp snaps over the pipe and grips the cloth.
Move to the opposite side and pull the fabric smooth and taut before snapping that clamp.
Repeat for the remaining two sides, pulling taut diagonally before snapping each clamp.
Check the grain: the vertical and horizontal threads should run parallel to the sides of the frame. Readjust any clamp that has skewed the fabric.

items.symptom: The fabric slips or puckers when stitching
items.cause: The clamps were not seated evenly, or the fabric was not pulled taut before the clamps were snapped.
items.fix: Remove all clamps, smooth the fabric flat, and re-mount with the opposite-sides-first method.

items.symptom: The clamps leave an impression on the fabric
items.cause: The clamps gripped the same section of fabric for many sessions.
items.fix: Move the position of the clamps by 1 to 2 cm every few sessions. On delicate fabric, slip a strip of acid-free tissue under each clamp.

content.text: The Q-snap frame is the go-to frame for long stitching sessions, particularly on linen where a wooden hoop would leave a ring mark. The
method also works on evenweave and cotton canvas.
